newsitem.title: USA: Amgen's growth prospects dim - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Amgen's growth prospects dim - Barron's.

text.p: Growth prospects for biotechnology company Amgen Inc will likely diminish following a string of bad news about three of its drugs, said a columnist for the weekly financial tabloid, Barron's.

"Much as we admire its financial impeccability and other manifest qualities, our investment view of the company remains unenthusiastic," wrote Alan Abelson in his column published in the tabloid's latest edition. "The latest items of intelligence on (three of its drugs) only confirm our earlier conviction that growth prospects are dimming for Amgen."

On June 17, the company said it expected slower sales growth for its Epogen due to changes in the Medicare reimbursement plan. The drug stimulates production of red blood cells to help fight anemia in kidney dialysis patients.
Abelson said the first human trial of Amgen's obesity drug, Leptin, showed it was only slightly more effective than other drugs on the market.

He also referred to two articles and an editorial in the New England Journal of Medicine, which raised questions about the usefulness of Neupogen, which is used in cancer therapy to stimulate the production of red blood cells.
On Friday, Amgen's stock closed at 59-7/16 on the Nasdaq, in line with the previous day's close. Its year low is 51-3/8.
When the company made its Epogen sales forecast and released the results of the Leptin tests, its stock fell 3-1/2 to 58-5/8.
